@sepo-agent /answer 

I just changed the readme file to make it simpler. Think of who are the readers -- when they read it they do not need to know the technical details at first place right. 

So can you reflect and check if you should update the prompt in other places? (But also there should be some callout block to mention this limitation? 

Also this is somewhat worthy of adding to our rubrics for communication and documentation?

I agree with the direction: the README is the front door, so it should stay reader-first and defer setup trade-offs to deeper docs.

What I checked:

- README now gives a short setup path without over-explaining the auth model: [`README.md#L9-L23`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3168c34f92febe27f28cd393cb699ef1efb74920/README.md#L9-L23)
- The detailed trade-off already belongs in setup docs: [`setup-guide.md#L23-L50`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3168c34f92febe27f28cd393cb699ef1efb74920/.agent/docs/deployment/setup-guide.md#L23-L50)
- The quick start still has more detail than the README, which is okay because it is already one level deeper: [`quick-start.md#L3-L17`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3168c34f92febe27f28cd393cb699ef1efb74920/.agent/docs/overview/quick-start.md#L3-L17)

I would add one short callout, but keep it non-technical. Best place: under the README quick-start app install step, or possibly in quick-start instead if we want the README even lighter.

Suggested wording:

```md
> [!NOTE]
> Sepo can only run in repositories where the Sepo GitHub App is installed. If you choose selected repositories, add each repository before onboarding it.
```

For prompts: I would not add this directly to every route prompt. The current prompts already ask implement/fix-pr to make the smallest complete change and review to evaluate docs/workflow fit, but they do not encode this specific audience-first docs preference. That is exactly what rubrics are for.

I do think this is worth adding as a rubric, probably under `rubrics/communication/`, something like:

- `title`: Write audience-first documentation
- `applies_to`: `implement`, `fix-pr`, `review`
- `description`: User-facing entry docs should lead with the reader’s immediate task and avoid front-loading internal mechanics. Put technical details, trade-offs, and limitations in deeper docs or short callout blocks when they affect user decisions.

Suggested next step: update this PR with the short callout, and add/update the rubric through the rubrics update path after this preference is accepted.

Agreed on both points.

The callout should not go in the main README. The README should stay as the entry path for first-time readers. The better place is the technical/details layer, likely the existing “Known limitations” section in [`developer-notes.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/developer-notes.md#L24), with a short pointer from the setup guide if needed.

Suggested limitation callout:

```md
> [!NOTE]
> The hosted Sepo App path only works for repositories where the Sepo GitHub App is installed. If you use selected-repository installation, add each repository before onboarding it.
```

For the docs clarity pass, I would handle it as a focused `/fix-pr` or `/implement` follow-up:

1. Keep [`README.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/README.md#L9-L25) simple and reader-first.
2. Review [`quick-start.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/overview/quick-start.md#L1-L19) for setup clarity, but avoid front-loading auth internals.
3. Put auth trade-offs and setup prerequisites in [`setup-guide.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/deployment/setup-guide.md#L5-L43).
4. Add the limitation callout under technical details, probably [`developer-notes.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/developer-notes.md#L24-L31).
5. Do a pass over deployment docs for duplicated or overly technical first-read wording.

I also agree this should become a rubric: “write audience-first documentation; keep entry docs task-oriented, and move limitations/trade-offs to deeper docs or callout blocks.” That belongs in communication/documentation rubrics rather than hardcoded into every prompt.
